HMCI’s name.

Decks, videos, pages, reports. Without one creative owner, they look different. That weakens the trusted, neutral voice the SMUD proposal depends on.

What HMCI getsCreative ownership as the partnership grows.03 / 14
Speaker note

The proposed SMUD partnership spans government relations, commercial real estate and power, an AI infrastructure platform, SMUD and NVIDIA research, and IR² community reinvestment. Each creates public-facing material. Under the proposal, operators give $0.01 per verified kWh to a local 501(c)(3), with annual public reporting. A shared creative owner helps protect HMCI’s neutral voice.

Source & context
  • Regional AI Infrastructure Partnership details supplied by Antonie Lewis. Presented as proposed work, not an awarded engagement.

Speaker note

We build approved prompts and templates around HMCI’s sources, audiences and voice. Then we teach employees and partners how to use them through hands-on AI design sessions using their own work. The aim is practical ability: write a better brief, develop a design, judge the output and bring it back to HMCI’s standards before publication. Training also supports the Amplify education pillar.

What HMCI getsA clear start and a consistent creative partner.12 / 14
Speaker note

First we review the materials HMCI and its partners already use. Then we build the brand guide and prompt library. We put those standards into templates and a refreshed website, and train the team in AI design. The monthly creative retainer keeps the work moving, with a short report on delivery and next priorities. The first conversation defines the starting scope.

Source & context
  • Rollout sequence supplied by Antonie Lewis. No pricing, fixed timeline or output quota is assumed.
